findings.reason: The protected source is already the conventional constant-space dynamic program. It partitions valid colorings by whether the final two posts match, initializes the two-post states directly, and advances both states with one simultaneous assignment per post. The genuine concepts same and different make the recurrence interview-readable, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 276 and its Python integer-pair-to-integer contract. The Reference preserves the two painting rules, all three source examples and explanation presence, and all three source constraints, including the guaranteed 32-bit answer range.

The immutable native source is tied to verified submission 2064300971. It and the app-local source have identical zero- and one-post guards, same/different initialization, loop range, simultaneous recurrence, and final sum; only the LeetCode class wrapper differs.

The previous 32/128/512-post benchmark violated both n <= 50 and the guaranteed 32-bit result range. Legal 10/20/40-post, two-color tiers retain a 4x span and complexity-sensitive recurrence. The current source passes at +0.04 relative exponent and 1.07x largest ratio; a correct quadratic prefix-recomputation control passes every output but fails only scaling at +1.12 and 8.45x.

The Approach now derives the two-post initialization before the recurrence, proves that the two ending states are disjoint and exhaustive, accounts precisely for linear time and constant space, and separates one-post, two-post, one-color, and defensive empty-input behavior.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, preserving all three examples in order, the first explanation's valid and invalid arrangements, all three constraints, and an independently represented equivalent of the source visual.

coverage: All three authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact input and output facts.
The suite covers the minimum n and k values, maximum k at n = 1, maximum n with the only legal color, and a two-post result close to the guaranteed 32-bit ceiling.
Separate cases exercise the n = 1 guard, the complete n = 2 initialization, the first n = 3 transition, and multiple later recurrence transitions.
One-color behavior is checked on two posts, the first forbidden third post, and the maximum-length fence, including both the sole valid assignment and zero-answer outcomes.
Both same-color and different-color ending states contribute to reviewed multi-step examples with two and three colors.

Expected values were independently checked by exhaustive enumeration for every 1 <= n <= 5 and 1 <= k <= 4 pair, plus a suffix-state dynamic-programming oracle for the longer authored and benchmark inputs.
All 13 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; all three hidden rows remain performance-only benchmarks in benchmark.json.
